title: Complicated urine infection

items: A complicated urinary tract infection is a urine infection that has spread beyond the bladder, or that happens with a condition that makes it harder to treat.
Examples include a blockage, a urine tube, or a kidney infection.
Painful or frequent urination, fever, chills, and flank (side) pain.
Feeling generally unwell or confused in some people.
Urine culture and sensitivity, to find the germ and the right antibiotic.
A kidney ultrasound if you have repeat infections or the treatment is not working.
Your doctor will choose antibiotics based on your culture result.
Treatment may need to be given into a vein if you are unwell.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Drink enough fluid unless your doctor has asked you to limit it.
Tell your doctor about all past antibiotic courses.
Your doctor may check your urine again after treatment.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Fever with chills or flank pain that does not settle
Low blood pressure or very little urine passed
